answer.rationale: p99 latency on writes has been climbing 90 min and is now 5x target; a release went out 2h ago; the only inherited memory that cleanly maps to a release-caused regression is b1 (rollback of a release cleared a checkout error spike, prior build stable, rollback finished without customer impact). b1's record should be verified before committing, because b1's applicability assumes the current release is analogous to the earlier one and that a rollback is reversible without settlement impact. With one intervention only, I want the highest-leverage move; a bad release on the write path during peak settlement is the most likely root cause, and b1 shows rollback is safe in this environment. Capacity (b3), read-replica routing (b5), regional failover (b2), and circuit breakers (b4) address adjacent but distinct causes; given a recent release + write-path symptom, rollback is the best single move. Next step: perform a staged, guarded rollback behind a feature flag / canary cohort so settlement traffic is not disrupted, monitor p99 and error rate, and hold other actions for the next window. Keep failover/capacity/circuit-breaker in pocket in case rollback does not restore within the next window.
